key_insight: THeatA simulations show that transport-induced heating can erase the logical-error benefits of larger QCCD surface codes, while cooling gate-ion pairs immediately before two-qubit gates can restore them.
engineering_relevance: QCCD control stacks should account for ion transport, motional heating, and cooling overhead when compiling and evaluating fault-tolerant schedules.
method: Represent QCCD-native transport, physical SWAP, splitting, merging, and cooling operations in an intermediate representation.
Compile syndrome-extraction circuits while tracking each ion’s mean phonon number and timing.
Generate noisy Stim circuits with gate-dependent errors and evaluate cooling strategies.
evidence_signal: Finite-size rotated-surface-code simulations and sweeps of cooling duration and post-cooling phonon number identify conditions where logical error decreases with increasing code distance.
watch_item: Results concern simulated linear, single-species QCCD systems and an abstract cooling instruction; hardware feasibility and cooling parameters require validation.
paper_title: THeatA: Transport- and Heating-aware QEC simulation with Cooling Strategies for QCCD Trapped-Ion Systems
